title: The suspension of the two-point type is equivalent to the circle
author: The Univalent Foundations Program

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 588-591: the suspension of the two-point type is the circle. The proof (source lines 592-634) is a construction with two inductions and no delegation: it defines the two maps by the recursion principles with explicit values on the generators (both poles to the base point, the two meridians to the loop and to reflexivity, and the inverse map on the loop as the composite of one meridian with the inverse of the other), then proves one round trip by induction on the suspension, where the meridian case is turned by transport in path spaces into an equation that is then checked separately for each element of the two-point type, and finally proves the other round trip by induction on the circle, where the loop case is computed with the functoriality of the action on paths. Defining the two maps so that they are actually inverse and carrying out both inductions is the substance; the statement alone shows none of it.
